column9: Chinese Formed Police Unit Hosts Training for 27 Liberian Law Enforcement Officers (Linked to Project ID #90319)
column10: From May 20 to 30, 2014, the Chinese Formed Police Unit hosted a training on law enforcement capacity building and computer operations in Sinoe County, Liberia. Twenty-seven officers from the Liberia National Police, Bureau of Immigration and Naturalization, and the Drug Enforcement Agency attended the training. Afterwards, they donated supplies to the local police force, which is captured in Project ID #90319. The Chinese Formed Police Unit were in Liberia as part of the UN Peacekeeping Mission.

column9: Chinese Formed Police Unit Donate Sporting and Security Equipment to Sinoe County Police ( Linked to Project ID #90318)
column10: On May 30, 2014, the Chinese Formed Police Unit donated sporting goods and security equipment to the Sinoe County Police. This donation was made at the end of a law enforcement training run by the Chinese Formed Police Unit, which is captured in Project ID #90318. The monetary value of the donation is unknown.

column9: Chinese Government donates $250,000 USD in medical equipment as part of Action Brilliant campaign (linked to #60024)
column10: On June 6, 2018, a Memorandum of Understanding was signed between Chinese Ambassador to Madagascar Yang Xiaorong, and Madagascar's Minister of Public Health, Lalatiana Andriamanarivo, in which the Chinese Government agreed to a donation of $250,000 USD in medical equipment to the Malagasy Ministry of Public Health. The equipment was handed over on the same day.  This donation was part of the 2 week long "Action Brilliant" campaign that began in Antananarivo on May 31st, 2018 to offer free cataract treatment in the country. The equipment will be left in the Joseph Ravoahangy Andrianavalona Hospital. The Action Brilliant campaign may also be known as Bright Journey Project or Brightness Action campaign. As part of the program, 11 ophthalmic experts from China were sent to the capital in 2017 (see linked ProjectID#60024).

column9: Chinese Government dispatch 11 optometry experts to support the Light Action Campaign (Linked to Project ID#60023)
column10: On September 19, 2017, a memorandum of understanding (MOU) for the 'Light Action Campaign' campaign was signed by Chinese Ambassador to Madagascar Yang Xiaorong and Malagasy Minister of Public Health Lalatiana Andriamanarivo. As part of the 2 week long program, 11 Chinese optometry experts were sent to the Antananarivo on May 31, 2017 to provide free cataract treatments to Malagasy patients. The goal of the campaign was to provide 200 free surgeries. Additionally, the medical equipment of the experts use was left at Joseph Ravoahangy Andrianavalona Hospital (see Project ID #60023). Because the project was only meant to run for 2 weeks, it is assumed to be completed.

column9: Chinese Government donates police supplies to Madagascar National Gendarmerie
column10: On August 20, 2019, the Chinese Ambassador to Madagascar, Yang Xiaorong, presided over a ceremony officially handing over a batch of police equipment to  Madagascar's National Gendarmerie. The ceremony was also presided over by General Richard Ratsimandrava, State Secretariat in charge of the National Gendarmerie. The exact nature of the donation is unknown, as is the value of the donation.  The donation comes as a part of Chinese investment in crime prevention in other countries. According to the Embassy, Madagascar's Gendarmerie had previously received Chinese assistance, in the form of training, as well as previous donations (see ProjectID#60916). The Gendarmerie is under Madagascar's Ministry of Defense.

column9: China Ministry of Public Security donates security materials for Madagascar Police Material Purchase Project
column10: On February 28, 2018, the Chinese Ambassador to Madagascar, Yang Xiaorong, took part in a signing ceremony for an Exchange of Letters Agreement with the Madagascar Ministry of Security. The letters specified that China's Ministry of Security would donate a batch of crime fighting materials to the Madagascar Ministry of Public Security. This agreement is seen as a way to strengthen diplomatic ties between China and Madagascar. This project is part of a continued investment on China's part in Madagascar's domestic security forces.   On July 25, 2019, the Government Procurement Office under the Chinese Ministry of Public Security announced a tender for the production of police equipment for the Ministry of Public Security Assisted Madagascar Police Material Purchase Project (Chinese project title: 公安部援马达加斯加警用物资采购项目). On September 6, 2019, China Machine International Tendering Co. Ltd. won the bid and will be carrying out the project for RMB 1.765 million (funded by China Ministry of Public Security). The equipment was to be delivered 51 days after the contract signing.  The equipment included 100 gas masks (RMB 480 each), 100 bulletproof vests (RMB 1,350 each), 100 police batons (RMB 300 each), 100 bulletproof helmets (RMB 1,200 each), 100 riot shields (RMB 160 each), 100 portable radios (RMB 2,860 each), 20 mobile radios (RMB 3,500 each), and 14 fixed long-distance transmission radios (RMB 57,500 each). China Machine International Tendering Co.also agreed to provide customers with free technical support, which includes: telephone support, on-site maintenance, replacement of spare parts, and regular inspections of customers.

column9: Chinese Embassy donates police equipment to Madagascar’s Ministry of Public Security
column10: On October 19, 2017, the Chinese Ambassador to Madagascar officially donated police equipment — including bulletproof vests — to Madagascar’s Ministry of Public Security. The monetary value of this donation is unknown.

column9: Chinese Embassy donates sporting goods to Madagascar State Secretariat of the Gendarmerie
column10: On February 22, 2018, Chinese Ambassador to Madagascar Yang Xiaorong, attended a ceremony commemorating the Chinese Embassy's donation of sporting goods to the State Secretariat of the Madagascar Gendarmerie. Landry Amaha Varisua, State Secretariat of the Gendarmerie of the Ministry of National Defense, and members of the Gendarmerie basketball team attended the ceremony. The donation appeared to include several basketballs, basketball shoes, and towels.

column9: Chinese Embassy in Madagascar donates materials to Malagasy National Gendarmerie
column10: On November 2, 2021, the Chinese Embassy in Madagascar donates materials to Malagasy National Gendarmerie (National Police Force of Madagascar). The donation included helmets and bulletproof vests. The monetary value of the donation is unknown.

column9: Chinese Government provides $8 million interest-free loan via ETCA for education and police projects (Linked to Project iD#52348, #57910, #69223)
column10: On January 21, 2016, the Chinese Government and the Government of Malawi signed letters of exchange for three separate projects: five community technical colleges (Project ID#57910), Mzuzu Youth Centre (Project ID #69223), and procurement of police vehicles (Project ID #57775).  Through these agreements, the Chinese Government signed letters of exchange for a soft loan of $8 million USD to support the five community technical colleges in Mzimba, Ntcheu, Zomba, Mulanje, and Nsanje districts. In addition to the loan, Chinese Government provided a $16 million grant to Malawi for the same project (Project ID #52348). The five community technical colleges project entered implementation on November 24, 2018. The contractor responsible for project implementation is China Railway 14th Bureau Group Co., Ltd. Around September 9, 2021, the company announced the completion of the project.

column9: Chinese government grants 100 vehicles worth $4 million to Malawi Police
column10: On May 18, 2016, the Chinese and Malawi governments signed an Economic and Technical Cooperation Agreement (ETCA) for the provision of police vehicles to Malawi. This agreement granted 100 vehicles, including pick-ups, sedans, SUVs and buses, worth $4 million to the Malawi Police, according to the MOFCOM source. On December 11, 2017, the Chinese government handed over the vehicles to the Malawi Police Service. Donated vehicles include two buses, three lorries, 10 minibuses, 10 station wagons, 15 saloons and 60 pickups._x000D_ _x000D_ On October 22, 2015, the Chinese government initially pledged to grant $2 million for the procurement of 100 police vehicles. However, the grant amount outlined in the Embassy article clearly states that $4 million was granted for the vehicles.

column9: Chinese Embassy in Malawi donates motorcycles worth K20 million to police
column10: On June 16, 2017, the Chinese embassy donated motorcycles to the Malawian police, according to the Chinese Embassy. According to the Malawi Times, 14 motorcycles were donated at a value of K20 million.  Around 100 people attended the ceremony, including Ambassador Wang, the Minister of the Interior and Internal Security, Chiumia, The Secretary-General of the State, Madura, and police chief Kachama, among other government officials and police officers.

column9: Chinese government sends 20 Malawian police officers for training in China
column10: From May 31, 2016 to June 29, 2016, the government of China funded 20 Malawian police officers to train at the Zhejiang Police College in China. On July 1, 2016, a welcoming ceremony was held for 20 Malawian police officers who received training in China. The cost of the training is unknown._x000D_

column9: Chinese embassy donates computers to Malawi police headquarters
column10: On December 7, 2011, Chinese embassy donated computers to Malawi police headquarters in Lilongwe. The value and amount of these computers is unknown.

column9: Chinese embassy grants computers and 10 motorcycles to the Lilongwe Police
column10: On August 2, 2010, Chinese embassy granted computers, rain jackets and 10 motorcycles to the Lilongwe Police. The value of this donation is unknown.

column9: Chinese embassy donates sports equipment to Malawi Police
column10: On November 17, 2008, the Chinese embassy granted sports equipment to the Malawi Police. The value of the donation is unknown.

column9: China donates office supplies to the Malawi Ministry of Defense in 2019
column10: On April 8, 2019, Ambassador Liu Hongyang met with Deputy Defense Minister Amos Melosi to exchange views on strengthening military relations between the two countries and to donate office supplies to the Ministry of Defense. China will continue to strengthen military relations through assistance, training, and cooperation to achieve new results. Melosi spoke highly of China's long-standing support for Malawi's national defense construction and thanked the Embassy for donating office supplies to the Ministry of Defense, and pledged to continue to promote military cooperation between the two countries. The monetary value of the donation is unknown.

column9: China donates newly constructed K188 million Nsipe Police Post to Malawi in May 2021
column10: On May 18, 2021, the Chinese government donated a newly constructed Nsipe Police Post to the Government of Malawi. The Nsipe Police Post, located in the Ntcheu District, will be used to assist Malawi in its reduction of road accidents and crime. It will serve a population of about 80 thousand Malawian people from Traditional Authorities Kwataine, Makwangwala, and Champiti. The Nsipe Police Post is worth K188 million.   The donation occurred at a handover ceremony, where Chinese Ambassador to Malawi Liu Hongyang and Malawi Vice President Saulos Chilima were in attendance. In addition to the Nsipe Police Post, the Chinese government also donated furniture, five motorbikes, and a refrigerator to assist the new facility.

column9: Chinese Government provides security equipment to Malawi police force in April 2021
column10: On April 29, 2021, the Chinese Government donated security equipment to the Malawi police force. The equipment included 300 tents, bullet proof vests, handcuffs, gas masks, shields, helmets, shock baton sticks and binoculars. The donation has a monetary value of MK200 million ($250,000 USD).   A handover ceremony was held for this donation in Lilongwe, the capital of Malawi. Malawi’s Minister of Homeland Security, Richard Chimwendo Banda, and China’s Ambassador to Malawi, Liu Hongyang, attended the ceremony.

column9: The Chinese Consulate General in Kuching donates 99,000 masks to the Federation of Sarawak Chinese Associations in June 2021 (linked to project #96941, #96942)
column10: In June 2021, the Chinese Consulate General in Kuching donated 99,000 masks, or a total of thirty boxes, to the Federation of Sarawak Chinese Associations. Consul General Cheng Guangzhong led the staff of the Consulate General to donate masks to the Federation of Sarawak Chinese Associations.  This was part of a series of donations to various entities in Sarawak State, Malaysia, in June 2021. Other donations include 201,000 masks (67 boxes) to the Sarawak State Disaster Management Committee (see project ID #96941) and a total of 380,000 masks to the Immigration Bureau, Police Station, Fire and Rescue Bureau, charity organizations, and other sectors of Sarawak (see project ID #96942).

column9: The Chinese Consulate General in Kuching donates 201,000 masks to the Sarawak State Disaster Management Committee in June 2021 (linked to project ID #96940, #96942)
column10: In June 2021, the Chinese Consulate General in Kuching donated 201,000 masks to the Sarawak State Disaster Management Committee (a total of 67 boxes) to support medical workers and other front-line anti-epidemic personnel. Minister of Local Government and Housing of Sarawak Dato' Seri Sim Kwai Hsien received supplies on behalf of the Sarawak Disaster Management Committee.   This was part of a series of donations to various entities in Sarawak State, Malaysia, in June 2021. Other donations include 99,000 masks (30 boxes) to the Federation of Sarawak Chinese Associations (see project ID #96940) and a total of 380,000 masks to the Immigration Bureau, Police Station, Fire and Rescue Bureau, charity organizations and other sectors of Sarawak (see project ID #96942).

column9: The Chinese Consulate General in Kuching donates 380,000 masks to various sectors of the Sarawak government (linked to project ID #96940, #96941)
column10: In June 2021, the Chinese Consulate General in Kuching donated 380,000 masks to various sectors of the Sarawak government, including the Kuching Airport Immigration Bureau, Police Station, Fire and Rescue Bureau, charity organizations and other sectors of Sarawak. The staff of the Consulate General donated the masks directly.   This was part of a series of donations to various entities in Sarawak State, Malaysia, in June 2021. Other donations include 99,000 masks (30 boxes) to the Federation of Sarawak Chinese Associations (see project ID #96940) and a donation of 201,000 masks (67 boxes) to the Sarawak State Disaster Management Committee (see project ID #96941).

column9: China donates 150 police motorcycles worth RMB 2 million to Maldives Police Service
column10: On August 16, 2014, an exchange of letters between Maldives and China was signed that stipulated that China was to provide 150 police motorcycles to the Maldives Police Service. On January 20, 2015, the Chinese Embassy to the Maldives handed over the donated motorcycles to the Maldives Police Service in Malé, Maldives. The estimated cost of these motorcycles was RMB 2 million, according to the Maldives Police Service. _x000D_ _x000D_ The vehicles were intended to help strengthen Maldivian law enforcement. The Maldives Police Service stated that the motorcycles would allow the police to perform their duties more efficiently and swiftly. According to Miadhu, the majority of the motorcycles were to be sent to different islands to improve their police service.

column9: China funds scholarships for 20 Maldivian police officers to attend seminar in China
column10: On April 7, 2014, a farewell ceremony was held in Maldives for 20 officers to go to China for a seminar on police service. The program was held from April 10 to April 24.

column9: Chinese Government donates a sea ambulance to Maldives National Defence Force
column10: In 2014, during Xi Jinping's state visit to the Maldives, he pledged that the Chinese Government would donate a sea ambulance to Maldives. Then, in 2015, during the visit of President of Maldives Abdulla Yameen Abdul Gayoom to China, the Maldives and China formally agreed to gift a sea ambulance to the Maldives. The sea ambulance was handed over to the Maldives National Defence Force (MNDF) on July 12, 2018. _x000D_ _x000D_ Additionally, Chinese Ambassador to Maldives Zhang Lizhong pledged that China would provide the required technical assistance for the boat. A Chinese expert team trained the Maldivians in ambulance driving and use of the medical equipment. Training was completed by October 30, 2018. _x000D_ _x000D_ According to the Edition, the donated sea ambulance was larger and featured more medical facilities than the existing 25 Maldivian sea ambulances. The 26-meter-long vessel was equipped with a “mini-medical theater,” including facilities for scans, electrocardiography tests, intravenous therapy, and oxygen delivery. The Chinese Embassy reported in July 2018 that the ambulance would improve the health and well-being of the Maldivian people. Many Maldivians live on remote islands and have poor medical conditions, so the ambulance would greatly improve the ability to transport and treat them. According to the Edition, medics had encountered drawbacks while transferring emergency patients from the atolls to Malé because of the length of travel, and the donation of the fully-equipped sea ambulance would help alleviate this problem. The Coast Guard was to manage to the new vessel.

column8: United Nations Multidimensional Integrated Stabilization Mission in Mali (MINUSMA)
column9: Chinese Government sends peacekeeping medical workers and engineers to join the United Nations Multidimensional Integrated Stabilization Mission in Mali (Linked to Project ID#87024)
column10: On December 3, 2013, the People's Liberation Army (PLA) sent 135 peacekeepers to Mali to join the United Nations Multidimensional Integrated Stabilization Mission in Mali (MINUSMA). The peacekeeping force, drawn from troops based in Harbin, China, consisted of 35 engineers, 65 medical workers, and 35 soldiers. For the soldiers involved in this peacekeeping detachment, see linked project ID#87024; the engineers and medical workers are captured by this project. The Chinese peacekeepers arrived in Bamako, Mali on December 4, 2013 for an eight-month long mission. More peacekeepers arrived later; ultimately, 365 Chinese peacekeepers served between December 2013 and the mission's completion in August 2014. The peacekeepers were set to work on repairing roads and bridges and providing medical assistance, while the security forces were to guard MINUSMA's headquarters and barracks. This was reportedly the first time the PLA sent security forces on a peacekeeping mission.

column9: Chinese Embassy donates sewing machines and other materials to the Malian Military Family Association
column10: On September 20, 2019, the Chinese Embassy in Mali donated sewing machines and other materials to the Malian Military Family Association. The materials were handed over by Ambassador Zhu Liying.

column10: ZTE Corporation China donated two B.T.S. radio sets (Model ZXC10) worth Rs. 4,960,000 to the Mauritius Police Department, specifically the Communications Branch.  The date of donation is listed as April 5 2012.

column9: Chinese Government donates printers, laptops, TVs and other equipment valued at Rs. 675,000 to the Mauritius Police Force
column10: In 2012, the Chinese Government donated 15 system unit Lenovos, 15 flat panel monitor Lenovos, 10 HP Printers, 5 Lenovo laptops, 2 LCD Hisense TVs and 1 Konika TV to the Mauritius Police Force. These items have an estimated value of 675,000 Rs. The donation was received on June 5, 2012.

column9: Chinese Government donates electronic equipment to the Mauritius Police Force
column10: In 2012, the Chinese Government donated equipment to the Mauritius Police Force, listed as: diagnosis equipment for an MG6 vehicle, a Samsung laptop, a charger, a mouse, and laptop carrying case worth Rs. 30,000. The donation was received on October 24, 2012.

The ceremony was attended by Mauritius Police Chief Connaught and Counselor Song Yanqun. The specific materials donated and the value of the donation is unknown.

column8: Mauritius Ministry of Social Security, National Solidarity and Environment and Sustainable Development
column10: On and around June 5, 2018, the Chinese Government provided the Flood Control and Disaster relief techniques and management for developing countries training to the Ministry of Social Security, National Solidarity and Environment and Sustainable Development of Mauritius. Two Mauritian officials received training in this project (pg.284 of "Statement of Foreign Aid Received for the financial year 2017-2018").

column9: Chinese government donates COVID medical materials to Mauritius
column10: On July 23, 2020, Chinese Ambassador Sun Gongyi and his wife Wang Ju handed over anti-epidemic materials donated by the Chinese government to the wife of the Prime Minister of Mauritius, Kobita Jagannath, on behalf of first lady Peng Liyuan. The handover ceremony took place at the treasury building in Port-Louis, the capital of Mauritius.  The donated materials included medical protection gear, face masks, and body temperature scanning devices.   The supplies were donated at the request of the Organization of African First Ladies for Development. The donation to Mauritius was part of a larger series of donations to 53 African countries sent on the behalf of first lady Peng Liyuan.    The Mauritian Ministers of Social Integration, Social Security and National Solidarity, and Gender Equality and Family Welfare, as well as several female parliamentary representatives were also present at the handover ceremony.

column9: Chinese Embassy donates reflective vests to the Mauritius Police Force
column10: On July 14, 2016, the Chinese Embassy donated a batch of reflective vests to the Mauritius Police Force.

column9: China Zhejiang Police Academy Holds Special Training Class for the Mexican police
column10: In July 2017, the China Zhejiang Police Academy will hold a special training class for the Mexican police in July. On 30 June 2017, the Ambassador to Mexico went to the Chinese Embassy in Mexico to prepare the Mexican police for their travels to China for training.

column9: Chinese Government provides USD $425,000 worth of anti-epidemic supplies to the Mexican Institute of Security and Social Services of State Workers in June 2020
column10: On June 25, 2020, the Chinese government donated 100,000 surgical masks, 20,000 PPE suits, 20,000 N95 masks, 20,000 infrared thermometers, 10,000 goggles, and 20,000 face shields to the Mexican Institute of Security and Social Services of State Workers (ISSSTE). column9: Chinese Government donation of police uniforms to FSM in 2017

column9: China donates medical equipment worth 8 million RMB to Mongolia
column10: On July 24, 2002 the Defense Ministry of China donated medical instruments worth 8 million yuan to the Military Central Clinic of Mongolia.

column9: Ministry of Defense of China grants 2 million RMB worth of Police Equipment to Mongolia
column10: On May 4, 2017, Chinese Ambassador Haiming Xing, representing the Chinese Government, handed over a donation of equipment from the Ministry of National Defense of China to the Mongolian Police. The donation includes Iveco minibuses, gas masks, and police equipment, and is worth 2 million RMB in non-refundable aid.

column9: Chinese Government provides RMB 10.3 million grant for provision of supplies and equipment to support the 11th ASEM Summit
column10: On January 5, 2016, Chinese Government and the Government of Mongolia signed letters of exchange, which committed RMB 10,395100 of grant funding for the provision of furniture and  audio-visual equipment — including simultaneous interpretation equipment, fire-fighting equipment, police equipment, large conference tables, sofas, and podiums — to support the 11th ASEM Summit in July 2016. column9: Chinese Ministry of Public Security donates medical supplies to General Police Department of Mongolia
column10: On May 13, 2020, the Chinese Ministry of Public Security donated medical supplies including masks, protective clothing, goggles, and other anti-epidemic materials to the General Police Department of Mongolia to show support for the Mongolian police as they battle the pandemic. The monetary value of the donation is unknown.

column9: Chinese Government donates de-mining equipment worth $150,000 to Mozambique's Armed Forces
column10: On July 20, 2001 China delivered de-mining equipment to the Mozambique Defence Armed Forces. The equipment, which includes assorted mine detectors and protection gear for sappers, is worth more than 150,000 dollars.  Mozambican Defence Minister Tobias Dai said the equipment would be used in designated minefields so as to permit the implementation of socioeconomic projects.

column9: Chinese Government provides police equipment to Mozambique’s Ministry of Interior worth $3 million
column10: On March 2, 2005 the Mozambican Interior Ministry received a donation from China, valued at three million US dollars, intended to boost the capacity of the police force. The donation included 300 motorbikes, 500 helmets, bullet- proof jackets, and masks for the riot police, 100 large tents, with a capacity ranging from 36 to 100 people, 5,000 police uniforms, 6,000 torches for the traffic police, 25 computers, 15 fax machines, and even equipment for the police band. column9: China Eximbank provides RMB 300 million government concessional loan for Modern Customs Scanning Equipment Acquisition Project (Linked to project #1314)
column10: In December 2007, China Eximbank and the Government of Namibia signed an RMB 1 billion concessional loan framework (recorded in the linked project #1314), which identified several projects that would be funded according to a consistent set of terms and conditions. One of these projects was the Modern Customs Scanning Equipment Acquisition Project. This agreement was signed by China’s Ambassador to Namibia Ren Xiaoping and Nambia’s Minister of Finance Saara Kuugongelwa-Amadhila.   Then, in 2008, China Eximbank and the Government of Namibia signed an RMB 300 million government concessional loan (GCL) agreement for the Modern Customs Scanning Equipment Acquisition Project. The GCL carries the following terms: 20 year maturity, 5 year grace period, and 2% interest rate. The final loan maturity date, according to "Summary Report of the Auditor-General on the Account of the Government of Namibia for the Financial Year Ended 31 March 2014," is March 21, 2028. In May 2008, the Permanent Secretary of Finance (Mr. Carl Schlettwein) of the Government of Namibia signed a $55,348,800.00 contract with Nuctech Company Ltd for the purchase of 10 x-ray container scanners capable of detecting contraband at security crossings around the country. The Government of Namibia agreed to pay $12,828,800 up-front through an advance payment to Nuctech Company Ltd. The balance of the contract price ($42,520,000.00) was to be funded with the RMB 300 million loan from China Eximbank.   The Modern Customs Scanning Equipment Acquisition Project has been plagued by domestic political controversy and a criminal investigation regarding a possible kickback scheme involving the $12,828,800 advance payment. Anti-corruption investigators allege that, five days after the May 2008 contract was signed, Nuctech Company Ltd. secretly entered into a $12.8 million contract with Teko Trading CC (“Teko”), which is a company owned by two Namibians (Teckla Lameck and Jerobeam Kongo Mokaxwa). Teko was allegedly tasked with pushing for a higher price for the scanners and using their political access to “expedite prompt payments”, according to a copy of the contract submitted to a court in Namibia. Shortly after the securing the contract with Nuctech Company Ltd., Teckla Lameck (a former chairperson of Namibia’s Public Service Commission), Jerobeam Kongo Mokaxwa and a Chinese co-conspirator (Yang Fan) allegedly went on a spending spree, purchasing houses, farms, and cars. The pending criminal case is political and diplomatically sensitive because, at the time that these contracts were signed, Hu Haifeng (to son of President Hu Jintao) was the head of the Nuctech Company Ltd.

column9: Chinese Government provides RMB 200 million grant for Nepal Armed Police Force Academy Construction Project

The project involved the construction 19 individual buildings, including a teaching building, dormitory building, covered hall, indoor and outdoor training venue, canteen, stadium, and swimming pool. The training academy is located on a mountain slope at Chandragiri municipality on the outskirts of Kathmandu and it is the first of its kind in Nepal.   The construction of the training academy began on April 16, 2015, just a few days ahead of a devastating earthquake, and it was completed on May 15, 2017.  The official handover ceremony took place on June 30, 2017. An official inauguration ceremony took place on March 19, 2018.  The ceremony was attended by more 400 people, including Nepalese PM Ollie, Interior Minister Thapa, Armed Police Director Shreitas, Chinese Ambassador Yu Hong, Business Counselor Peng Wei, and the Chairman of the 14th Bureau of the China Railway.  Ollie thanked the Chinese Government for their contribution towards peaceful development in Nepal, starting with this new training facility. column9: Chinese Government provides RMB 117 million grant — via ETCAs — for National Emergency Operations Center (COEN) Construction Project (Linked to Project ID#36258, #73188, #36351, #62359, #36419, and #62921)
column10: Discussions between the Peruvian and Chinese governments about the National Emergency Operations Center (COEN) Construction Project started as early as 2012. Letters of exchange funding a feasibility study were signed April 6, 2013 (as captured via Project ID#62921). Letters of exchange to construct COEN were signed on November 12, 2014 by the Chinese Minister of Commerce and the Peruvian Minister of Foreign Relations. A design contract was signed with China International Engineering Design & Consult Co., Ltd. (CIEDC) (Chinese: 中外建工程设计与顾问有限公司) on April 22, 2015. Then, on August 26, 2016, the two governments signed an execution agreement for the construction of the National Emergency Operations Center, or Centro de Operaciones de Emergencia Nacional (COEN) in Chorrillos, Peru near Lima. The agreement committed RMB 117,630,000 in grant funding for the National Emergency Operations Center (COEN) Construction Project. The funds were drawn from the Economic and Technical Cooperation Agreements (ETCAs) that were signed by the two governments on August 20, 2012 (as captured via Project ID#36258), April 6, 2013 (as captured via Project ID#62359), November 12, 2014 (as captured via Project ID#36419); September 23, 2011 (as captured via Project ID#36351); and November 23, 2009 (as captured via Project ID#73188).  The purpose of the project was to construct the National Emergency Operations Center, or Centro de Operaciones de Emergencia Nacional (COEN) in Chorrillos, Peru near Lima. The construction area was 3,733.29 square meters. The center consists of a room for each of the modules, administrative offices, a crisis room, press room, an inter-sectoral coordination room to facilitate communication with the police and armed forces, meeting rooms, an international conference room, amenities for personal such as a gymnasium. The project also included a mobile command center.  Technical assistance was also provided through this project, including the provision of training for personnel who would work in the center and sending a technical team from China to help with the creation of the center.  The COEN's purpose is to monitor, validate and provide official information on dangers, emergencies and disasters for timely decision-making. It also included an Awareness, Simulation and Training Center, for both experts and members of the general public. COEN is part of the larger National Disaster Risk Management System (Sistema Nacional de Gestión del Riesgo de Desastres/SINAGERD). It is overseen by the National Institute for Civil Defense, or Instituto Nacional de Defensa (INDECI).   Yanjian Group Co. was the project's contractor, and one of their subsidiaries, Yanjian Group Peru SAC also participated in project implementation. The Peruvian Agency for International Cooperation (APCI) also helped with the project's implementation and the Agency of International Economic Cooperation of the Chinese Ministry of Commerce was also involved with project implementation, though the precise extent is unknown. About 90% of the project was funded by the Chinese government, with an additional 6,754,781 soles provided by INDECI on top of the grants from the ETCAs, including from INDECI’s Fund for Interventions in the Occurrence of Natural Disasters (Fondo Para Intervenciones ante la Ocurrencia de Desastres Naturales/FONDES).  Construction began on May 22, 2017. In 2017, the entrance tracks and the main structure of the building were completed, along with a trench and canal on the Surco River that passes through the construction area. By the end of 2018, the reception and installation of various equipment for operations -– such as LED screens, speakers, projectors, liquid crystal displays, and splicing displays for a GIS map and disaster scenes, among other items -- was completed.  Construction ended in 2019, with the official handover and unveiling ceremony taking place on July 18, 2019.

column9: Chinese Government donates first batch of riot gear to Royal Solomon Islands Police Force (linked to project ID#97214)
column10: On December 23, 2021, the Chinese Government agreed to donate riot equipment (captured via Project ID #93528) and provide six police liaison officers (captured via Project ID #93529) to equip and train the Royal Solomon Islands Police Force (RSIPF). The premier of Malaita Province, Daniel Suidani, even held an independence referendum in 2020, which the national government dismissed as illegitimate. Papua New Guinea and Fiji dispatched peacekeepers while New Zealand deployed police and troops.

column10: On June 8, 2020, China Electronic Technology Group Corporation (CETC) donated 149 non-contact digital thermometer guns and 2 non-contact smart access control cameras to Sri Lanka’s Ministry of Defence. The monetary value of this donation is unknown.

column9: Chinese Embassy in Sri Lanka donates materials valued 1.5 million rupees to the Seva Vanitha Unit of the Sri Lanka Air Force in November 2021
column10: On November 12, 2021, the Embassy of China made a donation of over Rs. 1.5 million to the Seva Vanitha Unit of the Sri Lanka Air Force. This was delivered by the Chinese delegation led by the Defence Attache of the Chinese Embassy in Sri Lanka, Senior Colonel Wan Dong. The purpose of this donation is to continue the dedicated work by the SLAF Seva Vanitha Unit to uplift the living standards of families of service and civilian personnel who are in need through welfare projects in the year 2022.

column9: Chinese Embassy in Sri Lanka donates 50 bicycles and 3 electric buggies to Sri Lanka Navy (SLN)
column10: On December 10, 2019, the Chinese Embassy in Sri Lanka donated 50 bicycles and 3 electric buggies to the Sri Lanka Navy (SLN). The purpose of the donation was to support the SLN's "Green and Blue environment" initiative that seeks to protect and conserve the environment  The Deputy Military Naval and Air Attaché of the Embassy of the People’s Republic of China in Sri Lanka, Lieutenant Colonel Chang Qianjin, handed over the bicycles and buggies to Commander of the Navy, Vice Admiral Piyal De Silva during a ceremony on December 10.  The Navy intends to use these bicycles and electric vehicles at the Naval Dockyard in Trincomalee.

column9: China sends 435 peacekeepers on UN mission to Sudan in 2005
column10: On September 8, 2005, China announced it would send 435 peacekeepers on a UN mission to help rebuild Sudan. The first batch of peacekeepers arrived in Sudan in October 2005. These 435 peacekeepers included a 275-man engineering unit, a 100-man transportation unit, and a 60-man medical unit, all of whom were from the Jinan Military Region. These peacekeepers' main assignment was to aid in the reconstruction of Sudan.   It is unknown when this peacekeeping mission ended: however, in 2007 another peacekeeping team was sent to Darfur (recorded in project #2402), and as of 2019 it was reported that China had sent a total of 15 engineering units to Darfur. However, where they were sent and how many engineers were in the units is unknown.

On May 10, 2018, the Chinese Ambassador to Sudan Li Lianhe and other Chinese and Sudanese officials attended a ceremony for the donation of agricultural and other production equipment to Sudan. Sudan’s Minister of Defence Aud, Chief of Staff of the Army Abdul Fatah, Undersecretary of the Ministry of Finance Mustafa, Director General of Foreign Financing Omar and Zhou Chunlin, Economic and Commercial Counselor of the Chinese Embassy in Sudan attended the ceremony. The donation was provided to the Popular Defense Forces as part of the Disarming and Demobilization program in rural areas. This program aims to help former rebels reintegrate into society. The monetary value of the donation is unknown.

column9: China donates security and safety equipment to Sudan customs
column10: On December 16, 2019, the Chinese Government signed an agreement with the transitional government of Sudan for the donation of security and safety equipment to the Sudan customs. The deal was signed between the Ministry of Finance and Economic Planning of Sudan and the Chinese Government. China also offered personnel training and technical services, to help Sudan crack down upon smuggling, enhance the capacity of customs clearance for both personnel and goods, and safeguard national security. The monetary value of the donation is unknown.

column9: China grants police materials to Suriname Customs
column10: On June 29, 2006, a letter of exchange was signed by Chinese Ambassador Chen Jinghua and Minister of Finance Humphrey Hilton Bach for the Chinese government’s donation of police materials to Suriname Customs. _x000D_ _x000D_ On May 17, 2007, a supply contract was signed. _x000D_ _x000D_ On August 20, 2007, the police materials were handed over to the Suriname customs agency. The materials are intended to assist the Suriname customs agency in preventing illegal smuggling.

column9: China donated 30 bulletproof vests to Suriname police headquarters (linked to #56298 and #56507)
column10: According to the Chinese Embassy in Suriname, on December 16, 2016, Chinese ambassador Zhang Jinxiong donated 30 bulletproof vests to the KPS (Korps Politie Suriname), the Suriname police department. The vests were received by the police director at the Suriname Police Headquarters. Additionally, the Chinese Embassy assisted in repairing patrol vehicles, offered training for some officers in China to strengthen police law enforcement capabilities (captured in #56507) and donated two police vans (#56298).

column9: China grants 2 police vans to Suriname's Police Department (linked to #56253 and #56507)
column10: According to the Chinese Embassy of Suriname, on March 17, 2017, China granted 2 police vans to the KPS (Korps Politie Suriname), the Suriname police department. The goal of this donation is to improve law enforcement and ensure security in Suriname. The value of the two vans is unknown.  According to Starnnieuws, in April 2017, four instructors from China arrived to train ten members of the KPS in how to operate the 2 police vans. This information was confirmed via the KPS website, which stated that the training was conducted on April 7th, 2017. China has worked with the KPS in the past and donated 30 bulletproof vests to them 3 months prior to this donation (#56253). Additionally, the embassy will send Surinamese police officers to train in China to strengthen local law enforcement (captured in #56507)

column9: Chinese Government donates medical equipment to Military Hospital 601
column10: On March 22, 2017, the Chinese Embassy in Syria donated 90 wheelchairs and 40 crutches to Military Hospital 601 (المشفى العسكري or المستشفى العسكري "601") in the city of Damascus.

column9: Chinese Ministry of Public Security grants aid worth $640,640 to Tajik Ministry of Internal Affairs
column10: In 2002, the Chinese Ministry of Public Security and the Tajik Ministry of Internal Affairs (also known as the Ministry of the Interior) signed an agreement on the fight against terrorism, extremism and separatism, which included the provision of no-strings aid to Tajikistan. The aid was handed over on March 11, 2003. The aid consisted of twenty patrol cars (Radio Free Europe suggests it was 50 vehicles), special equipment, computers, laser printers, uniforms and footwear for the ministry's special subdivisions, special crime detection equipment, communication devices, night vision binoculars, cameras, metal detectors, shields, and helmets, among other goods. Material for bomb defusal was also included. _x000D_ _x000D_ Media sources indicate that the value of the aid was $700,000. However, according to the Flat Export from Tajikistan AIMS as of May 2018, the Chinese government funded "Policemen facilities" (AIMS project ID TJK/042056) worth $483,600. Additionally, there was an additional contribution of $157,040 USD for "Different kind of equipment" (AIMS project ID TJK/042058). Together, these two donations totaled $640,640, therefore it seems they are referencing this same project, even though transaction amounts differ slightly, so the transaction amount was coded as $640,640 USD to reflect official source information.

column9: China-funded Takuriabu Anti-drug Branch office building
column10: On March 18, 2016, Yue Bin, the ambassador to Tajikistan, attended the completion handover ceremony of the office building of the China-funded Takuriabu Anti-drug Branch office building. The project was funded by Ministry of Public Security of China and implemented by China Jing'an Import & Export Corporation. The office building aided by the Chinese side is a three-story brick-concrete structure with a construction area of ​​more than 1,000 square meters, including offices, equipment rooms, interrogation rooms, lounges.

column9: Chinese Government provides RMB 70 million grant for automobiles, munitions, and special technical equipment
column10: In 2017, China committed to grant technical facilities worth 70 million RMB to Tajikistan to strengthen its capacity of emergency response. Committee of Emergency Situations and Civil Defense secured automobiles, munitions, and special technical equipment from China through an agreement under the United Nations Development Programme. It was estimated that Tajik authorities would begin to receive this assistance around September/October of 2017.  More than 100,000 people live in danger areas in Tajikistan, and 27 people have died in natural disasters in the first half of 2017. As of July, 2017, 284 areas in Tajikistan were considered dangerous for human habitation. Along with the project, the Committee will also receive $500,000 grant from Japan and $460,000 from Russia.

column9: Chinese Embassy donates communications equipment to Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Tajikistan
column10: On August 23, 2018, the Chinese Embassy donated communications equipment to the Tajik Ministry of Foreign Affairs. The equipment included communication stations and intercoms to improve working conditions. The donated batch of communication equipment was expected to improve Tajikistan's diplomatic reception capabilities and its security. The value of the donated items is unknown.

column9: Chinese Ministry of Public Security provides RMB 4.5 million grant for police materials
column10: On October 13, 2010, the Ministry of Public Security of the People's Republic of China donated police equipment worth RMB 4.5 million to the the Government of Tajikistan. China Jing’an Import and Export Corporation (also known as China Jing An Import and Export Corporation or 中国京安进出口公), which is a major state-owned arms and materials supplier to China’s security services, was the contractor responsible for implementation. No further implementation details are available.

column9: Chinese Ministry of Public Security provides RMB 20 million grant for police patrol cars, police communications equipment, and computers
column10: In 2013, the Ministry of Public Security of the People's Republic of China provided a grant worth RMB 20 million to the Government of Tajikistan for the provision of police patrol cars, police communications equipment, and computers to Tajikistan’s Ministry of the Interior, Narcotics Administration and National Security Commission. The police patrol cars, police communications equipment, and computers were officially delivered to the local authorities on or around November 21, 2013.

column9: Chinese Ministry of Public Security provides RMB 3 million grant for police equipment
column10: On April 25, 2011, the Ministry of Public Security of the People's Republic of China and the Government of Tajikistan signed an RMB 3 million grant agreement for the provision of police equipment. No further implementation details are available.

column9: China Donates Police Vehicles to Tanzania
column10: On March 17, 2003, China donated five Toyota vehicles worth 200,000 USD to the Tanzanian police force to strength it's capacity. Commissioner of Police Wilson Mwansasu and Chinese Chief Economic and Commercial Representative Yu Yingfu were in attendance.

column9: China Donates Information and Computer Technology Facilities for Interior Ministry
column10: On November 27, 2008, the government of China donated $1.5 million USD worth of computer equipment to the Tanzanian Ministry of Home Affairs. The donation given by China's Deputy Minister for Public Security, Cai Anji, and to the Ministry of Home Affairs Deputy Minister, Khamis Kagasheki, consisted of 50 desktop computers, 30 laptops, scanners, and digital cameras.

column9: China Donates Computer Equipment to Tanzania's Ministry of Home Affairs
column10: On 5 September of 2009, the Chinese Ministry of Public Security made another computer donation to the Tanzanian Ministry of Home Affairs. Worth about 1.5 million CNY, the donation included 150 personal computers, 50 notebook computers, 30 scanners, and 40 digital cameras. The donation was haded to Tanzanian Minister of Home Affairs Lawrence Masha.

column8: Dar es Salaam Special Zone Police
column9: Changzhou City Police Bureau Donates Laptops to Tanzanian Police
column10: On November 24, 2012, the Police Bureau of Changzhou City donated ten laptops to the Dar es Salaam Special Zone Police for facilitation of combating crime. The donation was worth an estimated 15 million Tanzanian shillings.

column9: Chinese Government grant for Moshi Police Academy Expansion Project
column10: On March 22, 2017, a Chinese Embassy official signed a project implementation agreement with a Tanzanian Government representative for the Moshi Police Academy Expansion Project. The monetary value of the grant commitment from China’s Ministry of Commerce (MOFCOM) that support this project is unknown.  The Chinese Government originally financed the construction of the Moshi Police Academy back in the 1960s, and the facility was in need of renovation and expansion. The total construction area was 5,500 square meters consisting of 1 office building, 2 teaching buildings, and 4 dormitory buildings. It was equipped with computers, projectors, desks and chairs and other teaching equipment. Jiangsu Construction Group was the contractor responsible for project implementation. Construction began on June 1, 2017 and was completed on December 12, 2018. The official handover ceremony took place on April 10, 2019.

column9: China donates 50 motorcycles to Tanzania Police Force
column10: On June 23, 2014, China's Vice Minister of Commerce Li Jinzao attended a ceremony to donate 50 motorcycles to the Tanzania Police Force. This came as part of the "Second China-Tanzania Investment Forum."

column9: China donates office supplies to the Zanzibar Police Station.
column10: On October 17, 2019, the ceremony of a donation of office supplies to the Zanzibar Police Station by the Consulate General in Zanzibar was held at the Zanzibar Police Station. The donation included some computers and other office equipment, and was made to improve office conditions and improve work efficiency. The value of the donation is not known.

column9: Chinese Government donates office equipment to Police Region 5 in Thailand
column10: On December 11, 2018, on behalf of the Chinese Government, Chinese Ambassador Ren Yisheng donated office equipment, such as computers and projectors to Police Region 5 of the Royal Thai Police. Region 5 consists of the northern Thai city of Chiang Mai.

column9: The Chinese Embassy in Thailand donates masks to Thai government institutions and hospitals
column10: On April 5th, 2020, the Embassy of the People's Republic of China in the Kingdom of Thailand donated N95 and disposable masks to the Palace Affairs Office, the National Assembly, the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, the Airport Customs, the Airport Administration, the Airport Immigration Bureau, and various police stations, as well as Ratchaviti Hospital and Sirirat Hospital. The quantity sent to each institution is unknown.

column9: China deploys 11th civilian police peacekeeping team to Timor-Leste
column10: On March 27, 2007, China sent a group of 10 civilian police officers to Timor-Leste to help the country stabilize following its crisis in May 2006. They were accompanied by three military observers from the UN mission in Timor-Leste (UNMIT). The officers are specialists in the fields of administrative management, information technology, public security, criminal investigation and border security. They have received training in weapons, driving, and languages in China's peace-keeping police training center. _x000D_ _x000D_ On September 25, 2007, the team received UN peace medals for their efforts in Dili. Together, they represent the 11th civilian peacekeeping team that China has sent to Timor-Leste.

column9: China deploys 14th team of peacekeeping police in Timor-Leste
column10: China's 14th peacekeeping squad to Timor Leste arrived in 2009. The 21-person squad was sent to work with the UN mission in East Timor for one year, setting the end date to be in February 2010. Seven out of the 21 members had previously participated in UN peacekeeping missions. The squad, which includes staff from the criminal investigation, public security, traffic and entry and exit sections in the southeastern Jiangxi Province, all passed strict exams in the regional situation, world affairs, international law, driving, first aid, and English.

column9: 15th Chinese Deployment of Peacekeeping Police Timor-Leste
column10: China sent its 15th deployment of peacekeeping police officers to Timor-Leste May 11, 2010. The team comprised of 24 members from the province of Shandong with backgrounds in criminal investigation, public security, and traffic control. Like previous teams, the Chinese police officers will be working with the UN mission in Timor-Leste to help stabilize the country. Eight out of the 24 police personnel had previously participated in United Nations peacekeeping missions.

column9: 17th Chinese Deployment of Peacekeeping Police in Timor-Leste
column10: On May 16, 2012, China deployed its 17th batch of police officers to Timor-Leste to support the UN peacekeeping operation in the country. The team comprised of 13 officers from the Chinese province of Heilongjiang and would be staying for six months to support law enforcement efforts in Timor-Leste. The team formally began their work on May 22, 2012 and returned to China November of the same year. Prior to their tenure, the team underwent nine months of training in preparation for their mission.

column9: 16th Chinese Deployment of Police Forces in Timor-Leste
column10: On May 11, 2011, China sent its 16th deployment of peacekeeping forces to Timor Leste. This squad comprised of 23 members from the Department of Public Safety of Fujian Province. Member had received training from the Chinese Peacekeeping Police Training Center in topics such as situation identification, international law and peacekeeping behaviors. They will replace the 15th deployment from Shandong Province and will complete a year long mission in Timor Leste with the United Nations. The 16th batch of Chinese peacekeepers would return to China at the end of 2012.

column9: Chinese Government donates communications equipment worth $75,000 to Timor-Leste’s Ministry of Home Affairs
column10: On September 8, 2005, the handover ceremony for the Chinese donation of police supplies and communications equipment to Timor-Leste was held at the Ministry of Home Affairs (援助东帝汶内政部警用物资). Chinese Ambassador to Timor-Leste Chen Duqing and Minister of Home Affairs Rogerio Lobato [罗热里奥·洛巴托] handed over the police supplies (captured in #64675) and communications equipment from the Chinese Ministry of Public Security, and both signed the transfer certificate. According to Timor Leste's 2006-07 General Budget of the State, the funding for the communications equipment amounted to 75,000 USD.

column9: China donates logistic materials to the Timor-Leste Defense Force (FDTL) in 2019
column10: On August 14th, 2019, the handover ceremony of logistics materials occurred at the Timor-Leste Defense Force, FDTL (Falintil-Forcas de Defesa de Timor-L'este) headquarters. The FDTL headquarter was built with Chinese aid in 2010 (see project #38001). Ambassador Xiao Jianguo of China attended the ceremony, emphasizing that the provided logistics materials will improve the self-sustaining capability of the F-FDTL and improve the living conditions of military officers/soldiers. The handover certificate was signed by Ambassador Xiao and Minister Filomeno.

column9: Chinese Government donates police uniforms worth $110,000 to Timor-Leste’s Ministry of Home Affairs
column10: According to Timor Leste's 2006-07 General Budget of the State, the funding for the China's donation of police uniforms amounted to 111,000 USD. On September 8, 2005, the handover ceremony for the Chinese donation of police supplies and communications equipment to Timor-Leste was held at the Ministry of Home Affairs [内政部]. Chinese Ambassador to Timor-Leste Chen Duqing and Minister of Home Affairs Rogerio Lobato [罗热里奥·洛巴托] handed over the police supplies and communications equipment from the Chinese Ministry of Public Security, and both signed the transfer certificate.

column9: China completes well-drilling project for TLDF barracks in 2018
column10: On February 6th, 2018, the completion ceremony for the Timor-Leste Defense Force Bakao (Bacau?) well-drilling project (in Chinese, "东帝汶国防军包考军营打井项目") aided by the Chinese government was held at the Timor-Leste Defense and Security Ministry. The project was implemented by Shandong Foreign Economic and Technical Corporation (中国山东对外经济技术合作集团有限公司). The project will reportedly address water shortage issues for personnel stationed at the barracks and nearby residents. Signing and construction start dates are unknown.

column9: China donates security equipment to Timorese National Police in 2018
column10: On March 14, 2018, a ceremony was held at the Timor-Leste National Police Headquarters for the donation of security equipment from China to the Timor-Leste National Police. The donation included multi-functional command and control systems, digital trunking communication systems, explosives removal suits and alcohol testers, and other items. Chinese Ambassador to Timor-Leste, Liu Hongyang, and East Timorese Minister of Defense and Security, Somochu, signed the handover certificate on behalf of the two governments. The monetary value of the donation is unknown.

column9: China donates uniforms to Timor-Leste National Police in 2019
column10: On December 13, 2019, the handover ceremony of police uniforms from China for the Timor-Leste National Police was held at the Timor-Leste National Police Headquarters. Chinese Ambassador to Timor-Leste Xiao Jianguo and Minister of the Interior Filomeno da Paixão de Jesus signed the handover certificates on behalf of the countries.

column9: China sponsors training for Timor-Leste Police Officers in 2018
column10: On August 30, 2018, the "2018 Timor-Leste Police Law Enforcement Officer Training Course" (in Chinese, "东帝汶警务执法官员研修班") pre-departure education event was held at the Timor-Leste National Police Headquarters. The training was undertaken in China by the Yunnan Police Officers College. A total of 20 Timorese police officers attended the 15 days of training. The opening ceremony of the training was held at the Yunnan Police Officers College on September 3, 2018.

column9: Chinese Ministry of National Defense donates Covid supplies to the Ministry of National Defense of Timor-Leste in June 2020
column10: On June 25, 2020, the Chinese Embassy in Timor-Leste handed over Covid materials provided by the Chinese Ministry of National Defense to the East Timor Defense Ministry and the National Defense Forces. The materials will be used to help the Eastern Timor Defense Forces better combat the epidemic. The specific amounts and monetary value of this donation are unknown.  The handover ceremony was held at the East Timor Defense Force Headquarters.  Ambassador Xiao Jianguo, East Timor Minister of Defense, Commander of the National Defense Forces, and Defense Attaché to East Timor, Senior Colonel Huang Damin, attended the ceremony.

column9: Chinese government donates police supplies to Timor-Leste National Police
column10: On January 22, 2021, the Chinese government donated police supplies to the Timor-Leste National Police (PNTL). The donated supplies included boots, rainproof uniforms, and other goods. The handover ceremony took place at Timor Leste National Police Headquarters.

column9: China donates flashlights to Timor-Leste National Police
column10: On January 28, 2021, the Chinese government donated 200 flashlights to Timor-Leste National Police (PNTL). The handover ceremony took place at Timor Leste National Police Headquarters.

column9: Chinese Embassy donates detention center to Dili Police
column10: In April 2021, The Timor-Leste government requested help from the Chinese Embassy to construct a detention center. Construction took more than 6 months to complete. On December 17th, 2021, construction was complete and the Chinese Embassy handed over the center to National Police.

column9: China donates 3 billion CFAF worth of trucks and military engineers to Togolese Army
column10: On June 7, 2014, the Chinese Ministry of Defense held a ceremony for the donation of 3 billion CFAF worth of trucks and military engineers to the Togolese Army. The ceremony was attended by Liu Yuxi, the Chinese Ambassador to Togo. The donation aims to equip the Togolese Army to better respond to disasters such as flooding and plague, and assist in building schools and roads.

column9: China donates motorcycles and office equipment worth 37 million CFA in 2015
column10: On May 7, 2015, China handed over the donation of motorcycles, LED screens, computers, photocopiers, and fax machines to Togo. Chinse Ambassador to Togo, Liu Yuxi, and the Togolese Minister of Foreign Affairs, Robert Dussey attended the donation ceremony. The equipment was estimated to be worth 37 million CFA and was donated in preparation for the upcoming African Union Summit on Maritime Security and Development.

column9: China donates anti-malaria medication to Togo in 2017
column10: On December 8th, 2017, a handover ceremony was held for the donation of antimalarial medication to the Ministry of Health and Social Security of Togo by the Chinese Ambassador to Togo._x000D_ _x000D_ According to a deputy dean in charge of the Lomé Regional Central Hospital in Togo, artemisinin is the first choice for the treatment of malaria in the hospital. Every year, the Chinese government assists Togo with artesunate antimalarial drugs and conducts malaria treatment and training and guidance for local medical staff.

column9: Chinese Embassy provides supplies to Togolese Women's Organizations in September 2021
column10: On September 10, 2021, the Chinese Embassy in Togo and the Women's Movement of the Alliance for the Defense of the Republic jointly provided materials to the Togolese Women’s Organization. This donation was made to provide material assistance to women in need in Togo. The monetary value of this donation is unknown.  A material handover ceremony was held for this donation. China’s Ambassador to Togo, Chao Weidong, the Executive Secretary of the Alliance Party, the Vice Chairman, and representatives of women's movement members attended the ceremony.

column9: China grants office equipment to Tonga for the Pacific Islands forum (linked with projects #39235, #37641)
column10: On October 8, 2007, Ambassador Hu Yeshun handed over a batch of office supplies to Tonga to aid in their hosting of the 38th Pacific Islands Forum. This donation included 20 laptop computers, 10 computer desks, a laser printer, one fax machine, two photocopiers and 20 mobile phones. The donation, and forum, took place in Nuku'alofa. The value of this donation is unknown._x000D_ _x000D_ This project is linked to #39235, which records a donation of police motorcycles, and #37641, which records a donation of cars, both for the same forum._x000D_ _x000D_

column9: China military hospital ship provides medical services to Tonga (linked to project #65343)
column10: On August 13, the Peace Ark hospital ship of the Chinese People’s Liberation Army Navy arrived at the port of Nukualofa, Vuna Wharf in Tonga for a 7-day visit. While providing various medical services, the hospital ship also sent its medical team to local hospitals to carry out surgical operations in cooperation with the medical staff of Tonga, and set up medical teams to pay rounds of visits to remote islands and islets to provide diagnosis and treatment services. In addition, it also sent its teams to local schools and centers for the disabled to give diagnosis and treatment and carry out donation activities. The ship departed on Wednesday, 20 August after a week of providing free medical services that included 39 surgeries, including removing a bullet from a Tongan who had been shot while he was in the United States. Medical teams were also dispatched to the Vaiola Hospital. Patients on ‘Eua Island also received free assistance when a team flew to the island on board the vessel’s medical helicopter._x000D_

column9: China donated 20 police motorcycles to Tonga for the Pacific Islands Forum (linked to projects #37641, #37673)
column10: On September 28, 2007, the Chinese government handed over 20 police motorcycles to support Tonga's hosting of the 38th Pacific Islands Forum. The value of this donation is unknown. This project is linked to #37641 and #37673, which record donations of cars and office supplies for the same forum respectively._x000D_

column9: Chinese government donated a fire-fighting pick-up truck to the Tonga Minister of Police, Fire and Emergency Services
column10: On September, 22, 2017, Chinese Ambassador to the Kingdom of Tonga handed over a pick-up truck donated by China to Hon. Mateni Tapueluelu, Minister of Police, Fire and Emergency Services of Tonga. Minister Tapueluelu said the truck will be allocated to Ha'apai Fire Station. The truck is to improve the capabilities of the local fire service.

column9: Chinese naval hospital ship Ark Peace arrived at Tonga to provide medical service (linked to project #37762)
column10: On 13 August, 2018, the Chinese naval hospital ship Ark Peace arrived at Port Nukualofa, capital of the Kingdom of Tonga, the fourth stop of Mission Harmony 2018, starting an eight-day good-will visit and humanitarian medical service. Ark Peace paid her first successful visit to Tonga on the same date four years ago. (See project #37762)_x000D_ The Tongan government hosted a grand welcome ceremony at the Vuna Wharf. At the ceremony, the Acting Prime Minister Sika warmly welcomed Ark Peace's second visit to Tonga on behalf of the Tongan government and conveyed his appreciation to the ship for providing medical services to the Tongan people. _x000D_ Ambassador Wang pointed out that the second visit of Ark Peace, as an important part of events to jointly celebrate the 20th anniversary of the normalization of relations between China and Tonga, will further strengthen mutual trust and friendship between the two countries and the two armed forces.

column9: Chinese Embassy donates 12 motorcycles to the Tonga-China Friendship Association
column10: On June 27, 2009, the Chinese Embassy in Tonga donated 12 motorcycles to the Tonga-China Friendship Association. These motorcycles were set to be allocated to local police departments in six villages. The monetary value of this donation is unknown.

column8: Trinidad and Tobago Ministry of National Security
column9: Chinese Government provides TT$100 million grant -- via January 2020 ETCA -- for Forensic Science Center Construction Project (Linked to Project ID#69011 and ID#95316)
column10: On January 7, 2020, the Chinese Government provided a TT$100 million grant to the Trinidad and Tobago Ministry of National Security for the ongoing construction of the New Forensic Science Center in Mt. Hope. Grant funds were committed via an Economic and Technical Cooperation Agreement (ETCA) signed by the Minister of National Security and the Chinese Ambassador to Trinidad and Tobago (as captured via Project ID#95316).  The new building is expected to replace the current smaller one in St. James. The building is set to go up in two stages: first a new main forensic sciences building, and then a "L-shaped" DNA storage building. The new center is being constructed with the goal of alleviating personnel and infrastructure issues that have been plaguing the forensic department for some time.   The Trinidadians requested funding for the project from China after the Prime Minister visited a similarly Chinese-funded forensics center in Jamaica. As of January 2020, the project had not yet broken ground despite its proposed completion date by the beginning of 2020.   The 2020 grant represents additional funding for the project after the Chinese Government provided a $10 million dollar grant in 2018 (as captured via Project ID#69011).

column8: Government of the Republic of Trinidad and Tobago
column9: China Ministry of Public Security provides a 10-day police training course to Trinidadian law-enforcement agencies
column10: On November 16th, 2019, a team of instructors from Chongqing Police Academy began a 10 day training course titled "2019 Trinidad and Tobago Criminal Technology Seminar" for local Trinidadian police. The course was hosted by the Chinese Ministry of Public Security and was jointly organized by Chongqing Police Academy and the Trinidad and Tobago Police Academy. 30 officers from various branches of the Special Police Force and immigration border inspection participated in the training, which covered forensic inspection in the fields of technology, homicide investigation office, DNA inspection technology, criminal image processing, and drug inspection. The training course ended on November 26 after a closing ceremony attended by Ambassador Song Yumin.

column9: Chinese Government donates 200 motorcycles to the Trinidad and Tobago Police Service
column10: On August 21, 2019, Chinese ambassador Song Yumin formally presented a gift of 200 motorcycles to the Trinidad and Tobago Police Service (TTPS) at the Policy Academy in St. James, Port of Spain. The donation was originally announced on May 14, 2019. The motorcycles are equipped with GPS and camera technology, and the Prime Minister hopes that they will reduce the response time of the TTPS and give citizens a greater sense of security.

column8: Trinidad and Tobago Ministry of National Security
column9: Chinese Government provides grant via Economic and Technical Cooperation Agreement in January 2020 (Linked to Project ID#69175)
column10: On January 7, 2020, the Chinese Ambassador to Trinidad and Tobago and the Minister of National Security of Trinidad and Tobago signed an Economic and Technical Cooperation Agreement (ETCA). The ETCA provided an unspecified amount of grant funding and was to be used to finance both the construction of the New Forensic Science Center in Mt. Hope (captured via Project ID#69175) and "other projects agreed upon between both Governments."   The grant value likely exceeds TTD 100 million (about USD 14.8 million), given reports that the Prime Minister of Trinidad and Tobago announced TTD 100 million had been granted for the New Forensic Science Center.

column8: Trinidad and Tobago Ministry of National Security
column9: Chinese Embassy in Trinidad and Tobago donates intelligent conference terminals to Ministry of National Security in Trinidad and Tobago for digitization of government affairs
column10: On November 19, 2021, the Chinese Embassy in Trinidad and Tobago held a handover ceremony for the donation of intelligent conference terminals to the Ministry of National Security in Trinidad and Tobago. This ceremony was attended by Fang Yu, the Chinese Ambassador to Trinidad and Tobago, as well as Atiba Dirchang, the Secretary of the Ministry of National Security, and Lin Qi, the Deputy Director of the Department of International Affairs in Trinidad and Tobago. The purpose of this donation was to aid in the digitization of government affairs in Trinidad and Tobago. The monetary value of the donation is unknown.

column9: China Donates 90 Wheelchairs to Turkmenistanis with Disabilities throug NGO Yenme in 2018
column10: On December 18, 2018, the Chinese government donated 90 wheelchairs to children and adults with disabilities in Turkmenistan. The handover took place at an event hosted by Yenme, a public social welfare organization recognized by the United Nations operating in Turkmenistan. In attendance were China's Ambassador to Turkmenistan, Sun Weidong; Director Muhamedova of the Department of Disabled Affairs of the Turkish Ministry of Health, Director Ovetsova of the Social Services Department of the Ministry of Labor and Social Security, and Director Kasayev of the Ashgabat Social Services Bureau, as well as representatives from Yenme.

column9: Chinese Embassy in Uganda funded the construction of Uganda Police Department kindergarten project
column10: On January 7, 2014 the Chinese Ambassador, Mr. Zhao Yali handed over a Children Day Care Center to the Inspector General of Police, Gen. Kale Kayihura at Naguru, Kampala.  The China-Uganda Friendship Kindergarten was constructed by the Tian Tang Group and donated by the Chinese Embassy to the Uganda Police Force. The center will cater to Police Officers’ children who stay and work within Kampala.  The total cost of this project is unclear.

column9: China Poly Group donated 96 machines to Uganda Police Uniform Factory
column10: In 2014, the Chinese company, China Poly Technologies Inc, donated 96 machines worth $800,000 to the Ugandan Police garment factory and send technicians to train local employees. The factory will enable the Police to produce their own uniforms and at a later stage, supply other security organizations.  The Inspector General of Police, Gen. Kale Kayihura, said the factory would in addition to providing uniforms for the Force create jobs, especially for spouses of Police officers and tremendously reduce costs of uniforms.  He noted that the factory, which currently has a capacity of producing 100 uniforms per day, will, with time, be able to produce more than 200 uniforms per day.  The facility will reduce the cost of uniforms from $27 to $24 each.  There are over 200 people working in the factory producing over 260 suits of uniforms everyday.

column9: Chinese Embassy in Uganda donated office supplies to Uganda International Police Organization
column10: On December 30, 2014 the Chinese Ambassador to Uganda Zhao Yali donated office supplies to the Uganda International Police Organization.   The total cost of the donation is unclear.

column9: China donated motorcycles and laptops to Ugandan Police Darpartment
column10: On August 29, Ambassador Zhao Yali and U.S. Police Chief Kei Hula attended the Chinese Embassy’s donation of the Ugandan Police Department’s material handover ceremony. The donated materials include motorcycles and laptops.　　_x000D_ _x000D_

column9: China Tianjin International Economic and Technical Cooperation Group Corporation donated 1200 mosquito nets to UPDF and two schools in Uganda
column10: On April 8, 2016, the ribbon-cutting ceremony of the mosquito repellent net factory jointly established by China-Africa Medical Materials Co., Ltd (中非医用材料有限公司) and Tianjin Yongkuo International Trade Co., Ltd.(天津永阔国际贸易有限公司) was held in Kampala. At the ceremony, the mosquito net factory also donated 1200 long-lasting mosquito repellent nets to the UPDF and the two schools.

column9: Chinese Embassy donates a 22-seater bus to the Ugandan International Police
column10: On August 14, 2018, Zheng Zhuqiang handed over a 22 - seater bus to Uganda Police Force at function held at the offices of Directorate of INTERPOL and International Relations in Kololo, Mabua road.  The Deputy Inspector General of Police, Brig. Sabiiti Muzeyi thanked the Chinese embassy for its continued support towards Uganda Police Force.

column9: Chinese Government agrees to send a team to train the Ugandan police in December 2017
column10: On December 20, 2017, during a meeting between the Inspector General of Police, Kale Kayihura, and a delegation of the China Public Security, the Chinese Government agreed to send a team to Uganda to train the Uganda police in areas of criminal investigations, crime intelligence, and cybercrime. The decision was made after two Chinese nationals were murdered in Uganda.
