column9: Chinese Government provides RMB 20 million grant for provision of medical equipment to Ukrainian Ministry of Defense
column10: On November 22, 2013, China’s Ministry of National Defense and Ukraine’s Ministry of Defense signed an exchange of letters, which committed RMB 20 million of grant funding for the provision of medical equipment. According to the agreement, China’s Ministry of National Defense was responsible for transportation costs and delivery of the medical devices. Any additional costs were to be covered by the Government of Ukraine.   The equipment package consisted of 22 medical devices, including a phthalmic excimer laser, photocoagulators with different wavelengths used to treat retinal diseases, an angiograph, an optical coherence tomograph, an endothelial microscope, an optical biometer, a computer perimeter, a frequency doubling perimeter (for the full list of devices, see the source, ""Угода між Міністерством...""). The ultimate purpose of the project was to provide highly specialized ophthalmological care to wounded servicemen and patients of Holovnyy Viysʹkovyy Klinichnyy Hospitalʹ (Національний військово-медичний клінічний центр «Головний військовий клінічний госпіталь») in the capital city of Kyiv.   The equipment arrived at Boryspil International Airport in December 2015. The total weight of the equipment was 11.89 tons. The volume of the equipment is 28.23 cubic meters. The equipment arrived at the ophthalmology clinic of Holovnyy Viysʹkovyy Klinichnyy Hospitalʹ or around January 20, 2016.

column9: China Ministry of State Security donates masks to Ukraine in April 2020
column10: On April 10, 2020, 20,000 three-layer medical masks and 1,000 N95 masks donated by China's Ministry of State Security were held in a warehouse in Beijing to be loaded onto a plane to Ukraine. The supplies were eventually delivered to Ukraine.

column9: Chinese Government donates forensic equipment worth RMB 1 million
column10: In November 2002, China's Ministry of Public Security committed a donation of forensic laboratory equipment worth 1 million RMB to their Uzbek counterparts. The current state of this project is unknown. According to Chinese source, the contract is signed in 2001._x000D_ _x000D_

column9: China Commits to Give Uniforms worth US$150,000 to Uzbekistan's Police
column10: In February 2015, the Ministry of Public Security of China signed an agreement to provide uniforms (summer and winter clothing) to Uzbekistan's Ministry of Internal Affairs' policemen for a total amount of USD$150,000.

column9: Chinese Government grants RMB 700,000 for the provision of police equipment
column10: On November 26, 2004, Chinese Government signed an RMB 700,000 grant for the provision of police equipment. Under the agreement between the Ministry of Internal Affairs of the Republic of Uzbekistan and the Ministry of Public Security of the People’s Republic of China, the Chinese government granted 700,000 RMB to the Ministry of the Internal Affairs of the Republic of Uzbekistan.

column9: China agrees to provide training to Vanuatu police force
column10: During Vanuatu Prime Minister Serge Vohor's visit to China from September 5 to 12, 2004, China and Vanuatu signed an initial agreement that would provide equipment and training for the Vanuatu police force, following a request from the Vanuatu Minister of Public Utilities. Members of the police force will undergo training in China, particularly in anti-terrorism warfare and bodyguard and self-defense skills. Details regarding the agreement and further project details are unknown.

column9: China finances Vanuatu for police projects (Linked to Project ID#63871)
column10: According to a media report on August 2, 2005, China's People's Liberation Army and Vanuatu Police Force signed an agreement recently to finance police projects worth more than US$286,000. The funds also provided a 28-seater bus and three double cabin vehicles for use by the police force. A December 2005 Quarterly Economic Report by the Reserve Bank of Vanuatu confirmed that the agreement was worth US$319,000 and reached in July 2005.  During the same meeting, another aid agreement was signed between China's People's Liberation Army and the Vanuatu Mobile Force (VMF), which includes uniforms and equipment for the VMF (captured in Project ID#63871).

column9: Chinese Army provides medical training and service through the ‘Peace Ark’ Naval Hospital Ship to Vanuatu
column10: On August 31st, 2014, the Chinese Navy Ship, Peace Ark, arrived in Vanuatu to provide medical services. The ship served as the main platform for free-of-charge medical services, including "outpatient and surgical treatment" (according to "驻瓦努阿图大使谢波华在中国海军和平方舟医院船甲板招待会上的致辞"). The Chinese press release, "驻瓦努阿图大使谢波华陪同瓦总理参观和平方舟医院船", stated that the boat has received a total of 7,512 outpatients, completed 58 operations, admitted 26 inpatients, carried out 3382 CT and X-ray auxiliary examinations, and conducted comprehensive medical examinations for 33 people. Additionally, medical teams were dispatched to local hospitals and villages. The ship left on September 7th after completing its service. The arrival of the Peace Ark is heralded as one of the biggest bilateral events between the two nations.

column9: Chinese government donates equipment for Pekoa Airport to Vanuatu
column10: In 2005, the Chinese government donated $700,000 worth of equipment to the Peoka Aiport in Vanuatu, located in the city of Luganville on Espiritu Santo, the largest island of Vanuatu. According to page AIII-vi of "The Dragon Looks South," the equipment included x-ray machines to improve security screening, a baggage conveyor, and fire equipment. The exact start and end dates are unclear.

column9: Chinese government donates 14 military vehicles to Vanuatu to be used by specialized units of Vanuatu's Mobile Force
column10: In February 27th, 2017, China donated 14 military vehicles to be used by specialized units of Vanuatu's Mobile Force (VMF). The aim of this donation is to boost the country's capacity to deal with emergencies.    The donation includes includes transport vehicles, medics to evacuate casualties, vehicles for official use and other equipment to be used at the base, VMF workshop. Along with the vehicles, the police also received uniforms and safety equipment ("China Provides Vanuatu Mobile Force With 14 Military-Designed Vehicles").   According to Papua New Guinea Today, "the donation included vehicles, 3 troop carriers, 2 medium buses, 2 fully equipped recovery vehicles, 4 B90 sedan cars, 2 fully equipped ambulances and a fire truck," and is worth approximately 8 million RMB. The donation also included new uniforms and safety equipment.

column9: China government donates Military Band Music Equipment to Vanuatu
column10: On January 13th, 2016, the Chinese Ambassador, Xie Bohua, a ceremony was held for the donation of musical instruments to the Vanuatu Mobile Force (VMF) (or 捐赠瓦机动部队乐器). The VMF is the paramilitary arm of the country's police force. The ceremony was also attended by 30 officers and soldiers, including the Mobile Band Commander.  These instruments are intended to help the Vanuatu Mobile Forces military band renew and upgrade their instruments, and help the military band to better rehearse and perform for major events.

column8: Vanuatu Department of Customs and Inland Revenue
column9: China donates customs inspection equipment to Vanuatu in 2020
column10: On June 4 2020, a handover ceremony was held for inspection equipment from China to Vanuatu Department of Customs and Inland Revenue.  The donation includes CT baggage scanners, mobile x-ray system from Nuctech and is delivered by CCOEC. The equipment is to be used to improve border security, detection and seizure of illicit drugs, and prevent smuggling into Vanuatu.

column8: Banco de Desarrollo Económico y Social de Venezuela (BANDES)|China-Venezuela Joint Fund
column9: [China-Venezuela Joint Fund] Merida Cable Car Modernization Project (linked to #58677)
column10: The China-Venezuela Joint Fund financed the Merida Cable Car ("Teleferico de Merida") Modernization Project. The commitment date of funding for this project is unclear.   The China Development Bank has provided three tranches and one long term facility to the Joint Fund in total (#58677). FONDEN also contributes to this fund, and it's administered by BANDES. The first commitment to this fund was made in 2007.  The Mérida cable car one of the longest and highest cable car systems in the world. In August 2008, the Mérida cable car was shut down to protect user safety because it had reached the end of its service life. In 2010, the Venezuelan government hired the Austrian Doppelmayr company to modernize the Mérida cable car system. The modernization project included upgraded wagons, towers, safety devices, communication and security systems, seats for the disabled, an anti-slip floor, escape routes, and stairs. The new wagons have an increased capacity of 60 people per trip compared to the previous 40 people per trip. The Merida Cable Car reopened on 29 April 2016 in the pre-commercial stage for for children, the elderly and people with disabilities and reopened to the public on 7 October 2016.

column9: Chinese Ambassador to Venezuela gifts books to the Minister of Defense
column10: On October 15, 2015, during a meeting between Chinese Ambassador to Venezuela, Zhao Bentang, and Venezuelan Minister of Defense, Vladimir Padrino Lopez, Ambassador Zhao gifted Minister Padrino a Spanish version of the Chinese book "The Chinese Dream and the World".

column9: China donates 1st shipment of anti-epidemic materials to Venezuela in March 2020
column10: On March 19, 2020, the first shipment of anti-epidemic materials from China arrived in Venezuela. The shipment included 4,000 early diagnosis test kits, as well as materials used to administer these tests such as biosecurity suits, protective goggles, gloves, and air purifiers to support Venezuelan health care systems. The shipment arrived at Simon Bolivar International Airport in Caracas.

column9: Chinese Ministry of Public Security provides anti-epidemic supplies to the Ministry of Public Security of Vietnam in September 2020
column10: On September 14, 2020, Counselor Zhao Wanpeng of the Chinese Embassy in Vietnam provided anti-epidemic materials to the Ministry of Public Security of Vietnam on behalf of the International Cooperation Bureau of the Ministry of Public Security of China. Major General Jian Ling, the deputy director of the Foreign Affairs Bureau of the Ministry of Public Security of Vietnam, received disposable medical masks, goggles, and protective clothing.

column9: Chinese Embassy in Vietnam contributes reading room and Chinese books to Foreign Affairs Bureau of the Ministry of Public Security of Vietnam in 2020
column10: On November 3, 2020, the Chinese Embassy in Vietnam assisted the Foreign Affairs Bureau of the Ministry of Public Security of Vietnam by providing a reading room and Chinese language book corner. A ribbon-cutting ceremony for the reading room was held on November 3, 2020.   Minister Counselor Yin Haihong was invited to attend and cut the ribbon with Lieutenant General Nguyen Thanh Son, Director of the Vietnam Foreign Affairs Bureau. In addition, Minister Counselor Yin Haihong presented Chinese books such as "Xi Jinping: The Governance of China" to Vietnam on behalf of the embassy. Counselors Zhao Wanpeng, Wang Ben, Zhang Yi, and Director Zhu Yu of the Chinese Embassy also attended the ceremony.

column9: Chinese Embassy Establishes Sino-Vietnamese Cultural Reading Room and Donates Books to the Police Academy
column10: On January 1, 2021,  a ribbon-cutting ceremony was held for the new Sino-Vietnamese Cultural Reading Room of the Police Academy of the Ministry of Public Security of Vietnam. On behalf of the embassy, Counselor Yin Haihong also donated Chinese language books including "Xi Jinping on Governing the Country" to the reading room.

column9: Chinese Government donates computers, printers, and rain coats to the Zambian Police Service
column10: In 2003, the Chinese Government donated 10 computers, 10 printers, and 1,000 rain coats worth more than $60,000 USD to the Zambian Police Service.

column9: Chinese Government grants $8 million USD for provision of military and medical equipment
column10: On September 25th, 2013, the Chinese government signed a grant agreement providing $8 million USD (42.2 million ZK) to the Government of Zambia in the form of medical and military equipment to be used to upgrade military hospitals countrywide. Chinese Ambassador to Zambia Zhou Yuxiao explained that the delivery of the equipment would occur in three phases over the course of three years. It is unclear whether these goods were ever delivered.

column9: 18th military medical team dispatched to Zambia
column10: China has been sending military medical teams to Zambia since 1984. On January 20, 2015, China’s 18th military medical team arrived in Zambia. The 11-person team was stationed at Maina Soko Hospital in Lusaka and completed its term of service on January 18, 2016. The members of the team undertook outpatient service, consultation, operation, guidance and teaching activities at Maina Soko military hospital. They also provided medical care for the President and the First Lady, and treated hundreds of senior officials and officers from both Zambian government and military.

column9: Chinese Government provides training for Zambia's Golden Jubilee Celebration
column10: On May 22, 2014, China’s Ministry of Commerce sent a team to assist in the design and training of a choreography team for Zambia’s 50th Independence Day celebration (or “Golden Jubilee Celebration”) on October 24, 2014. At the request of Zambian Government, the China’s Ministry of Defense and the Chinese Armed Police also dispatched 7 instructors to train 500 members of the Zambia National Service for the much-anticipated independence celebration.

column9: ICBC provides $274.61 million loan for 2350-Unit Police and Security Force Housing Project
column10: In January 2016, the Government of Zambia and the Industrial and Commercial Bank of China (ICBC) signed a $274,612,768.07 loan agreement for the 2350-Unit Police and Security Force Housing Project. The proceeds of the loan were to be used by the borrower to finance 85% of the cost of a $323,073,844.79, three-year commercial (EPC) contract between the Government of Zambia's Ministry of Home Affairs and AVIC International, which was signed in December 2014. The Government of Zambia was responsible for directly financing the remainder (15%) of the project cost. As of July 2022, the ICBC loan had achieved a 97.9% disbursement rate ($268,959,363.78 out of $274,612,768.07).   The purpose of the project was to construct 2,350 housing units for members of Zambia's Ministry of Home Affairs: Zambia Police Service, Zambia Correctional Services, the Immigration Department, and the Drug Enforcement Commission. These housing units included 997 low-cost units, 1,238 medium-cost units, and 115 high-cost units. AVIC International and China 15th Metallurgical Construction Group Co. Ltd. were the contractors responsible for project implementation.  The project was implemented in two phases. Phase 1 was made up of four sites: Chelston in Lusaka (48 houses); Silverest in Lusaka, Chongwe area (41 houses); Kawama in Kitwe (24 houses); and Mukobeko in Kabwe (42 houses).   Phase 1 officially launched on October 27, 2015, but Phase 1 construction did not begin until July 7, 2017. Phase 2 construction activities ended on June 20, 2020. On July 29, 2022, the Ministry of Finance & National Planning (MOFNP) of Zambia announced that it was seeking lender approval to formally cancel the ICBC loan’s undisbursed balance ($5,653,404.29); however, it also noted that it had not yet secured formal lender approval for this action. This announcement came approximately 21 months after the Government of Zambia defaulted on its repayment obligations to Eurobond holders and approximately 6 weeks after China, France, and 14 other countries formed a creditor committee to discuss the Zambian authorities’ request for a debt treatment under ‘the Common Framework for Debt Treatment beyond the DSSI’ endorsed by the G20 and the Paris Club.

column9: China Eximbank provides $30 million loan for an unspecified defense project
column10: According to Zambia's Ministry of Finance, between January and June of 2018, China Eximbank and the Government of Zambia signed a $30 million loan agreement for an unspecified defense project. No further details are available.

column9: Chinese Government donates 180 solar water heaters to Zimbabwe Republic Police (ZRP) in 2006
column10: On August 24, 2006, the Chinese Government donated 180 solar water heaters to the Zimbabwe Republic Police as part of a project to introduce China's experience and technology in solar energy development to the solar energy-rich country.  The goal of this project was to evaluate the performance of the Chinese-made solar heaters under local conditions, to train local technicians in installation and maintenance, to demonstrate the green energy technology, and to promote commercial and industrial cooperation in green energy.  The pilot project, worth 1.5 million yuan (187,500 U.S. dollars), was completed in 1998, positively affecting the lives of 110 households.  The financial value of this second phase of the project is unclear.

column9: Chinese Government provides training for teachers from Zimbabwe Wushu Association (ZWA)
column10: In February 2013, China sent Wushu experts to train 63 local teachers in this form of martial arts at Chaminuka Training Centre in Mashonaland Central province. In August 2013, China was to select the top twenty teachers from the local school to travel to China and enhance their skills in Wushu martial arts. The selected teachers were to stay in China for one year.  The teachers arrived in China in November 2013 to study at Tianjin Huo Yuanjia Civil and Military School for African students. According to China Daily, the Zimbabwean students ended up studying Chinese more than Yushu. Zimbabwean Deputy Minister Dokora said the move to send the teachers to China reflected the good ties that the two countries enjoyed. “This is reciprocal and they too will be benefiting from English classes given by the Zimbabwe nationals,” he said. He said the program was being implemented in fulfillment of the China–Africa cooperation framework.  The ZWA president, Gilbert Makowah, said the Chinese Ambassador would also look at the prospects of getting some scholarships for Zimbabwean Wushu fighters. This training comes as a result of an agreement signed on 2 January, 2012, where the Chinese Embassy in Harare pledged development support for the Zimbabwe Wushu Association (ZWA).

column9: Chinese People's Liberation Army donates anti-epidemic materials in June 2020 to Zimbabwe National Defense Forces
column10: On June 4, 2020, anti-epidemic materials provided by the Chinese People's Liberation Army to the Zimbabwe National Defense Forces arrived at the Harareman Air Base in Zimbabwe. The materials included 62,000 masks, 19,000 pieces of personal protection equipment, and other critical medical supplies. China’s Ambassador to Zimbabwe, Guo Shaochun, the Minister of Defense and Veterans Affairs of Zimbabwe, and the Commander of the National Defense Forces attended the handover ceremony.

column9: Chinese Government donates personal protective equipment in August 2020 to Zimbabwe
column10: On August 27, 2020, Zimbabwe received a donation of personal protective equipment (PPE) from the Chinese government, which included tests kits, face masks, ventilators, and oxygen generators form the Chinese Government. The donation was presented through a virtual meeting by the Chinese ambassador to Zimbabwe to the President of Zimbabwe, Health and Childcare Minister, Defense and War Veterans Affairs Minister.
